WHAT THE SLOT WAS OFFERED FOR, AND WHAT IS BEING DONE WITH IT. The chairman's agenda §1.7 struck yesterday's next-steps item 9 (an order to 'FIRE ONE ARB/ ROW ON /cases/pending' as 'the cheapest open question in the project') after reading the relay corpus and finding the row already fired on 2026-09-07. THE SEAT INDEPENDENTLY RE-DERIVED THAT FINDING AND CONFIRMS IT: 579 rows across 75 result files; ten rows carry a /cases/pending URL; one of them is request 2026-09-07-daily.json, fetched_at 2026-09-07T12:18:11.313414+00:00, find 'ARB/', find_matched FALSE, status 200, 74431 bytes, sha256 ecbd32d6ee4dd42e..., outcome ok. The question item 9 said it would settle was settled 33 days ago in the negative. WHAT THE CHAIRMAN AUTHORIZED, AND WHY THE SEAT IS NOT WRITING IT AS AUTHORIZED. He authorized a narrowed thing: a corroboration of the ARB/ null 'at the CURRENT page state (untested; 198 bytes smaller than the state ARB/ was tested on)'. He expressly invited the seat to decline it or propose a better use of the same slot, and the seat PROPOSES A BETTER USE for two reasons. REASON 1 - THE AUTHORIZED DESIGN RESTS ON A PREMISE THE CORPUS REFUTES. The relay fires on the chairman's push, AFTER this session, so this batch cannot sample 'the current page state'. It will sample a FIFTH, as-yet-unobserved state. The corpus shows this page is not static across short intervals: 74431 bytes / sha ecbd32d6 on 09-07 and 74430 bytes / sha 712196ea on 09-09, one byte and a different digest 47 hours apart. So the honest description of what a second ARB/ row buys is 'a null on a second, different page state at least 33 days later', NOT 'a corroboration at a known current state', and this request says the former. REASON 2 - A SECOND SAME-URL NULL WOULD STILL BE THE REGISTER'S OWN WORD 'UNINTERPRETABLE'. open_threads[10] records, of this exact page, that "'ARB/', 'Netherlands', 'Subject of Dispute' and 'Subject' have ALL returned FALSE and the ONLY literal ever to match is 'ICSID', which matches in the page title and navigation chrome - so that page carries NO case-row prose as this relay retrieves it and its Wingtech null is UNINTERPRETABLE." Adding a second point to an uninterpretable series buys a series, not an interpretation. The chairman's own §8 ruling of 2026-10-09 names the cure: the right control on these ICSID docket pages is a literal that can ONLY occur in the region the target would occupy, because 'ICSID' proves only that a navigation menu was retrieved. THE DESIGN THIS SEAT SUBSTITUTES, FOR THE SAME ONE SLOT: A 2x2 CROSS-PAGE BRACKET, two region literals against two sibling pages, in ONE run. The target page is /cases/pending (region expected ABSENT). The control page is /cases/recent, which this corpus PROVES carries case-row prose that this relay's tag-strip surfaces: find 'ARB/' matched TRUE there in three rows (2026-09-07 idx8 sha 4af84337, 2026-09-17-zz-controls-and-databases idx2 and 2026-09-17-zzz-class-predicate-cure idx1, both sha 44e338a4) and the excerpts return ACTUAL CASE ROWS with party names, ICSID case numbers and dates - verbatim from 2026-09-07 idx8: 'na Faso (ICSID Case No. ARB(AF)/26/3) August 12, 2026 Plaza Centers N.V. v. Romania (ICSID Case No. ARB/22/15) July 28, 2026'. WHY A CROSS-PAGE CONTROL AND NOT A SAME-URL ONE, STATED RATHER THAN EVADED. The README rule is that every expected null needs a companion control on the SAME URL in the SAME run, and that rule is honoured below. But on a page whose target REGION is absent, NO same-URL region control can exist - the only same-URL literal that has ever hit is chrome. That is a logical limit of §8's criterion, not an exemption from it: the same-URL control can only ever establish RETRIEVAL on this page, and the REGION question therefore requires the same literal on a sibling page in the same run. Both are included and each is labelled with exactly what it can found. WHY 'ICSID Case No.' IS THE SECOND LITERAL, WITH ITS PRIOR ART STATED AND NOT CLAIMED AS NOVEL (the prior-art screen adopted 2026-10-07 applies to instrument claims, not only world claims). A census of the 'find' FIELD over all 579 rows returns 148 distinct literals. 'ICSID Case No.' has EXACTLY ONE prior row: 2026-08-20-daily.json idx2, on a THIRD icsid.worldbank.org page (the Decisions on Manifest Lack of Legal Merit register), where it matched TRUE at 94995 bytes and its excerpt returned a case row verbatim - 'Ioan Micula, Viorel Micula and others v. Romania (ICSID Case No. ARB/05/20) - Annulment Proceeding'. It has ZERO prior rows on /cases/pending and ZERO on /cases/recent. So the literal is ATTESTED as a case-row-region literal on this host rather than assumed to be, and it is stronger than 'ARB/' for this purpose because it cannot be satisfied by a stray designator outside a case row. PRE-REGISTERED EXPECTATION, FIXED HERE BEFORE FIRING AND NOT CHOOSABLE AFTER THE RESULT: rows 1 and 2 (both region literals on /cases/pending) return find_matched FALSE; rows 4 and 5 (the same two literals on /cases/recent) return find_matched TRUE; rows 3 and 6 ('ICSID' on each URL) return find_matched TRUE. WHAT THAT OUTCOME WOULD FOUND, IN THE HONEST FORM: that as retrieved at the batch instant, the tag-stripped, whitespace-collapsed rendering of https://icsid.worldbank.org/cases/pending contains neither of two literals that the SAME INSTRUMENT, in the SAME RUN, surfaces on a sibling docket page of the same site - which converts the 2026-09-07 null from 'uninterpretable' to 'a controlled negative on two independent region literals with a same-literal cross-page positive', and does so without any claim that a page lacking case-row prose lacks case rows.
